newsitem.title: USA: US pension funds can improve private equity -- study.
newsitem.headline: US pension funds can improve private equity -- study.

text.p: Public pension funds can improve their performance in the private equity market by addressing five problem areas, according to a pension fund study released Wednesday.

The study, sponsored by nine public pension funds, identified 30 terms and conditions that could be improved or added to private equity contracts in order to better align the interests of limited partners and general partners in private equity funds, sponsors of the study said at a press conference here.

"We think the study should spark a paradigm shift in the way investors participate in the private equity market," said Sheryl Pressler, chief investment officer of the California Public Employees' Retirement System (CALPERS).

Five problem areas cited by the study included misalignment of interests, the need for better disclosure, a lack of oversight by limited partners, high management fees and extra effort needed from general partners.
She said the private equity market, which consists mainly of venture capital funds and leverged buyout funds, was currently estimated to be around $100 billion.
Of that total, public pension funds account for about 20 percent, or $20 billion.

"We believe this study will be instrumental in heightening awareness of the need to obtain terms and conditions which protect limited partners and align interests with the general partners," said Gregory White, executive director of the Massachusetts Pension Reserves Investment Management Board.
He said the study included a recommendation that management fees should move from a flat fee structure to a budgeted or sliding fee schedule.
The study's sponsors included CALPERS, the Colorado Public Employees Retirement Association and the Massachusetts Pension Reserves Investment Management Board.
The Michigan State Retirement System, the Minnesota State Board of Investment and the New York State and Local Retirement System were also sponsors.
